corrected_finding.headline: The predecessor's claim that scene3d-ribbon-f1b-streaks.test.js (8/44) and scene3d-ribbon-wall-coverage.test.js (1/36) are PRE-EXISTING RED, 'not caused by the fix', is WRONG. This implementer disproved it.
corrected_finding.why_the_predecessors_proof_was_vacuous: Its 'pre-fix' comparison ran the SAME worktree test file with VECTURA_PRE_F1P=1 set — but neither scene3d-ribbon-f1b-streaks.test.js nor scene3d-ribbon-wall-coverage.test.js reads that env var at all (f1b-streaks reads a DIFFERENT flag, VECTURA_PRE_F1B, gated to its own d5af9e30 baseline). Setting VECTURA_PRE_F1P=1 while running those two files does nothing — both of the predecessor's 'pre-fix' and 'post-fix' runs executed the identical post-fix worktree code. Comparing a thing to itself and calling the match 'proof' is exactly the vacuous-comparison failure mode the protocol warns about.
corrected_finding.true_pre_fix_measurement: Built a scratch export via `git archive 8adfd5af | tar -x`, symlinked node_modules from MAIN, ran both files there (genuinely no wvPlaceCov present, grepped to confirm): scene3d-ribbon-f1b-streaks.test.js 44/44 PASS, scene3d-ribbon-wall-coverage.test.js 36/36 PASS. Both clean.
corrected_finding.post_fix_measurement: Same two files run in the shipped worktree (Prototype B): f1b-streaks 36/44 (8 fail), wall-coverage 35/36 (1 fail). All failures are on interlockWeave (7 of 8 in f1b-streaks + the 1 in wall-coverage) plus 1 additional interlockWeave-adjacent failure; trochoidLoop's lattice-sensitivity and streak-shape checks also fail (2 of the 8 in f1b-streaks), but far more mildly. onePenDown: 0 failures in either file.

trochoidLoop_numbers.degenerate: 0 (pre) -> 0 (post), no erosion failure here — this is a milder, different-mechanism dip

corrected_finding.root_cause_traced: surface-fill.js's ribbonize(), the erode()-then-fill path (~:7208-7228): under Prototype B, one CLS_RIBBON stretch's erosion produces an empty outline+fill multipolygon (a pre-existing FillBoolean/insetMultiPolygon robustness gap the plan's §9 already named, exposed here by B's changed geometry, NOT introduced by it). The code's own `if (!any) { ribbonRefuse('erodeEmpty'); outp.push(centrePass(st.a, st.b)); return; }` fallback IS taken — it does not leave a total void, it substitutes a bare single-pen centreline for that one stretch's usual full-width ribbon fill.
corrected_finding.visual_confirmation: Built a direct document-space PNG reconstruction of the ring polygons (blue), final ink (white), and uncovered cells (red) from the exact grid tests/helpers/scene3d-ring-coverage.js computes, for both the true pre-fix scratch export and the post-fix worktree. Pre-fix: clean zigzag pattern, ~5 stray red flecks (366 uncovered cells total). Post-fix: same pattern EXCEPT one ~25-30mm run of the family (2 clusters, 18.75mm2 + 17.65mm2 = 36.4mm2, together 99% of interlockWeave's 36.64mm2 reachable residue) renders as a THIN CENTRELINE (visible as a thin white zigzag line inside the red/uncovered overlay) instead of the neighboring stretches' full wide-ribbon fill.
corrected_finding.relationship_to_condition_2: This thinned stretch is very likely the SAME event as condition 2's own already-disclosed 39.81mm2 restated-bar cluster for interlockWeave (close in magnitude — 39.81 vs 38.95mm2 — and in document-space location, both ~x137-165/y71-98mm on this fixture). If so, this is not a SEPARATE undisclosed catastrophe — it is the already-priced-in condition-2 trade-off (Prototype B trades depth for area), just also visible through TWO OLDER guard files whose bars (ringFillRate>=0.995, ringNotInkMm2<3) were never re-pinned to accommodate that trade-off. Could not prove the two are the literal same polygon within this unit's budget.
corrected_finding.disposition: tests/unit/scene3d-ribbon-f1b-streaks.test.js and tests/unit/scene3d-ribbon-wall-coverage.test.js are OUTSIDE F1-placement's allowed-file scope (only tests/unit/scene3d-ribbon-flat-field-placement.test.js, the new oracle file, is allowed) — this implementer did not and could not re-pin their bars, per the 'do NOT try to fix it — outside your allowed files' instruction. Flagging for the orchestrator: either (a) grant scope to re-pin these two files' interlockWeave bars to match condition 2's already-ruled trade-off, or (b) rule that shipping Prototype B despite this fallout is/isn't acceptable as-is. This is the blocking item keeping this unit at MEASURED rather than DONE.
